  DualMirage: Hunting Stealthy Multimodal LLM Agents via CAPTCHAs with
                     Contour and Adversarial Illusions

                                Bei Chen         Gaolei Li*    Jun Wu       Jianhua Li
                                              Shanghai Jiao Tong University
                              {chenb2018, gaolei li, junwuhn, lijh888}@sjtu.edu.cn



                            Abstract

The rapid advancement of Multimodal Large Language
Models (MLLMs) has given rise to sophisticated au-
tonomous agents capable of performing complex, human-
like tasks across the web. However, this also introduces
significant security risks, particularly from stealthy MLLM
agents that can evade conventional detection mechanisms
by mimicking human behavior. In this paper, we propose
DualMirage, a novel CAPTCHA framework that proac-
tively counters and identifies stealthy agents by exploiting
fundamental disparities between human and machine per-
ception. DualMirage employs a dual-pronged strategy: (1)
Contour Illusions, which utilize cognitive principles to gen-
erate illusory contours that humans perceive effortlessly
yet pose interpretation challenges for MLLMs; and (2)                  Figure 1. Motivation of our proposed DualMirage. The first
Adversarial Illusions, which embed human-imperceptible                 mirage (i.e., contour illusion) creates a perception of non-existent
perturbations optimized to mislead the visual encoders of              contours (such as the Mona Lisa) for the human visual system
target MLLMs and thereby elicit characteristic, identifi-              through colorful stripes, while the second mirage (i.e., adversarial
able model responses. Evaluations on five state-of-the-art             illusion) hijacks the action of the multimodal agent, forcing it to
MLLMs demonstrate that DualMirage achieves an average                  reveal identity information (such as its model name).
95.8% human success rate while blocking MLLM agents
(up to 100% agent blocking rate), outperforming exist-
ing CAPTCHAs. Furthermore, DualMirage induces mod-                     pass access controls, orchestrate large-scale fraudulent ac-
els to expose identities actively, achieving 58.8% white-box           tivities, and manipulate public opinion. The ability of these
and 21.9% black-box attack success rates, proving effective            agents to “see” and “reason” about web interfaces as a hu-
against stealthy multimodal agents.                                    man would make them a potent, scalable threat to the in-
                                                                       tegrity of web ecosystems.

    Our core insight is to deploy two complementary types
of illusions simultaneously. 1) The first type of illusion is            2.1. Autonomous Multimodal LLM Agents
the contour illusion, which is “visible to the human eye, but            The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) into
invisible to the machine”. Studies on human vision show                  multimodal systems has catalyzed the development of au-

and visual reasoning, they lack the basic visual physiology              taught to use external APIs to extend their capabilities. This
unique to humans, and therefore cannot perceive illusory                 paradigm has been significantly advanced by frameworks
contours that humans can instantly recognize [4, 14]. 2)                 like WebGPT [27], which fine-tuned models to navigate the
The second type of illusion, adversarial illusion [3], oper-             web using a search engine and browser, and more recently,
ates on the opposite principle: “visible to the machine, but             by AppAgent [40], VisualWebArea [20], and WebVoyager
invisible to the human eye”. As a complementary tactic,                  [16], which systematically evaluate LLMs’ abilities to op-
we embed adversarial perturbations within the contour illu-              erate operating systems and complete complex tasks across
sion challenges. These perturbations are designed to be im-              websites. These agents typically function by ingesting vi-
perceptible to humans yet effectively mislead the MLLM’s                 sual and textual information from a screen, formulating a
visual encoder. Importantly, unlike traditional adversar-                plan, and executing low-level actions such as mouse clicks

aim to induce MLLM agents to produce a specific, verifier-               pirically demonstrated the powerful capabilities of multi-
intended output (such as its own model name), thereby forc-              modal agents in bypassing traditional CAPTCHA systems,
ing it to actively expose its non-human nature. By combin-               highlighting the need for next-generation verification mech-
